deployment_notes.local_vs_api_inference: Local inference (loading weights with `transformers` and running on your own machine) avoids per-request API costs and network latency, and keeps data on-device — but you pay for compute, storage, and maintenance yourself. API-based inference (calling a hosted model) trades that for simplicity, elastic scaling, and access to much larger models than most local hardware can run.
deployment_notes.model_selection: Pick the smallest model that meets the accuracy bar for the task. distilbert/distilgpt2-class models are fast and cheap for prototyping; move to larger models only if evaluation shows the smaller one underperforms on your actual data.
deployment_notes.gpu_cpu_considerations: CPU inference works fine for small models and low request volume (as used in this script). GPU inference becomes worthwhile once you're running larger models, batching many requests, or need low per-request latency at scale.
